value: 67 % of 43 scouts chose the branch leading to the plant carrying a septum with pure (E)-beta-farnesene against 33 % for the untreated control branch (n = 43, chi2 = 5.23, P = 0.02)
units: categorical (% of scouts choosing a branch, chi-squared against equal split)

source.authors: François J. Verheggen, Lise Diez, Ludovic Sablon, Christophe Fischer, Stefan Bartram, Eric Haubruge, Claire Detrain
source.title: Aphid Alarm Pheromone as a Cue for Ants to Locate Aphid Partners

method: behavioural: two-choice bioassay, scouts offered two plant branches, one plant carrying a rubber septum with pure (E)-beta-farnesene (EbF, the aphid alarm pheromone) and one untreated plant; one trial per scout
conditions: Queenless Lasius niger colonies (more than 500 workers) collected in Brussels in April 2007 and fed sucrose, dead arthropods and water; the Methods do not say whether ants were starved. Three colonies tested and pooled after the authors checked for bias; the number of scouts per colony is not given. 43 scouts, one trial each; septum placed alternately on either plant and switched after each scout, with similar replicate numbers on both sides. The septum dose is not stated. Same paper: in a four-arm olfactometer (30 scouts, one arm with five crushed Aphis fabae, about 50.9 ng EbF) 53.3 % of scouts first visited the EbF source against 25 % expected (chi2 = 9.63, P = 0.003) and spent 42.7 +/- 6.2 % of time there (F3,116 = 3.02, P = 0.033); the paper does not call the other three arms controls (filtered air only). Nulls in the two-choice test: time in the neutral area did not differ between EbF choosers and control choosers (F1,41 = 0.01, P = 0.978), walking speed did not differ (1.96 v 1.74 cm/s, P = 0.338) and hesitation before choosing did not differ (10 v 29 %, Fisher P = 0.190). Attraction to a single synthetic compound at an unstated dose; no detection threshold or non-detection disclosure beyond this.
quote: Ant scouts preferrentially orientated towards the branch leading to the EβF treated plant (67%) rather than to the branch leading to the control non treated plant (33%) (n = 43, χ2 = 5.23, P = 0.02).

value: only four individual cotton-seed compounds (1-heptanal, 1-decene, 1-nonanal, isopropyl palmitate) elicited significant attraction from both males and females in Y-tube olfactometer assays
units: categorical (Y-tube choice versus hexane control, chi-squared with Zc)

source.authors: Souvic Sarker, Ahmed M. Saveer, Pradeep Paudel, Aijun Zhang
source.title: Cotton Seed Volatiles Functioning as Host-Seeking Cues for the Oxycarenus hyalinipennis (Hemiptera: Lygaeidae)

method: behavioural: single-insect Y-tube olfactometer (glass, 5 mm internal diameter, 6 cm arms), 100 mL/min charcoal-filtered humidified air per arm, up to 5 min to choose; each of 17 headspace compounds at 0.1 ug against 10 uL hexane on filter paper
conditions: Bugs field-collected in October 2021 in Irvine, California and kept as a laboratory colony at USDA-ARS Beltsville (26 +/- 1 C, 75 % RH, 16:8 L:D); a choice needed at least 5 cm into an arm and 30 s residence. Individual compounds: 10 to 35 replicates for unmated and 10 to 32 for mated insects, one insect per replicate; mated and unmated pooled when they did not differ (p > 0.05); chi-squared tests, treatment and control arms alternated and filter papers replaced after each replicate, trial order randomisation not described. Per-compound results: males 1-heptanal Zc = 2.83 p = 0.005, 1-decene Zc = 4.42 p < 0.001, 1-nonanal Zc = 2.22 p = 0.027, isopropyl palmitate Zc = 2.63 p = 0.009; females 1-heptanal p = 0.008, 1-decene p < 0.001, 1-nonanal p < 0.001, isopropyl palmitate p = 0.001. In females p-xylene was repellent (p = 0.045), which the abstract sentence does not mention. Blends: the natural-ratio blend at 1 ug was not attractive to either sex (37.5 %, p = 0.317) and attracted both sexes at 0.01 ug (females 70.8 %, p = 0.004; males 71.4 %, p = 0.023); a blend lacking isopropyl palmitate attracted neither sex at any dose; several single-sex nulls at other doses. Odour attraction at a single dose, no threshold or non-detection measure; these are lure candidates, not a sensitivity estimate.
quote: Y-tube olfactometer assays revealed that only four individual compounds, 1-heptanal, 1-decene, 1-nonanal, and isopropyl palmitate, elicited significant attraction from both males and females.
note: Sentence read in two abutting pieces and the tail seen. Results (section 3.2) agree with the abstract figures. source.authors: Navapong Subpayakom, Pongrat Dumrongrojwattana, Supattra Poeaim
source.title: Chemosensory-Driven Foraging and Nocturnal Activity in the Freshwater Snail Rivomarginella morrisoni (Gastropoda, Marginellidae): A Laboratory-Based Study
source.journal: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens 6(4): 56

method: behavioural: two-sided tank test, opaque barrier with three 1.5 cm base perforations separating the bait side from the bait-free side, so only water-borne cues passed (barrier permeability checked with potassium permanganate)
conditions: Adult snails sieved from sand in four central Thai river basins (Bang Pakong, Pa Sak, Tha Chin, Mae Klong) on 26 to 29 March 2023, pooled and held at 25 C, fed-deprived for 3 days before trials. Each test used 3 independent tanks of 10 snails released at the tank centre, positions recorded every 15 min for 3 h (12 time points); the chi-squared tests used time-aggregated data, so the time points were not treated as independent, but the 3 tanks are the only replicates. About 400 mg dead shrimp (the paper names Macrobrachium lanchesteri in the food-choice section only) placed on one side; the Methods do not say how the bait side was chosen or whether it was randomised, and test order is not reported. Same paper: with a transparent barrier and no perforations (visual test) the split was 51.39 v 48.61 % (p > 0.05), and the light v dark choice was 51.67 v 48.33 % (p > 0.05). Exact p and test statistic for the chemosensory result are not given beyond p < 0.05; barrier perforations were large enough that snails might also have contacted bait, which the paper does not discuss. Attraction to a bait, no detection threshold or non-detection disclosure.
quote: The snails exhibited a strong preference for the bait-present side (98.06%) over the bait-absent side (1.94%) (Chi-square, p < 0.05).

value: the alfalfa volatile p-menth-8-en-2-one significantly attracted both male (chi2 = 5.786, df = 1, p = 0.016) and female (chi2 = 7.407, df = 1, p = 0.006) adults against a paraffin-oil control in Y-tube assays
units: categorical (Y-tube choice versus paraffin oil, chi-squared)

source.authors: Yingning Luo, Shuhua Wei, Fang Tang, Mark R. McNeill, Xiongbing Tu, Yanqi Liu, Chen Han, Changqing Qu, Xuewei Yin, Liping Ban
source.title: Identification and Evaluation of Alfalfa Volatiles for Monitoring and Management of Odontothrips loti and Frankliniella occidentalis

method: behavioural: glass Y-tube olfactometer (two 10 cm x 1 cm arms at 75 degrees, 50 mL/min air, dark room at 26 C), eleven synthetic alfalfa volatiles each at 10 ng/uL in paraffin oil against paraffin oil alone
conditions: Adults 3 to 5 days old from a laboratory colony founded from thrips field-collected in 2021 from an alfalfa field at the Shangzhuang Experimental Station (China Agricultural University), reared three generations on alfalfa leaves, starved 3 h before tests. Odour positions swapped after every five thrips, tube cleaned with 75 % ethanol after every ten; no formal randomisation described. Replicate number is ambiguous: Methods say 60 biological replicates for female and male per treatment, the Figure 3 caption says sixty in total for both sexes, and a Figure 4 caption gives 8 and 10. The other ten compounds elicited no significant response in either sex (same Results section). Dose series for this compound: O. loti females were tested at 1, 5, 10, 50, 100 and 1000 ng/uL and males at 10, 100 and 1000 ng/uL; at 10 ng/uL females responded 2.35 times and males 2.06 times more than controls (chi2 = 9.281, p = 0.002; chi2 = 6.564, p = 0.01). Electroantennogram responses showed no significant differences across the tested concentration range (df = 5, p = 0.598), so the EAG did not corroborate a dose effect. Attraction to a single synthetic compound at a screening dose, no sensitivity threshold. The same paper also tests Frankliniella occidentalis, not logged here.
quote: The assay results showed that p-Menth-8-en-2-one significantly attracted both male (χ2 = 5.786, df = 1, p = 0.016) and female (χ2 = 7.407, df = 1, p = 0.006) O. loti compared to the control (Figure 3, Table S6).

source.authors: Kevin Farnier, Noel W. Davies, Martin J. Steinbauer
source.title: Not Led by the Nose: Volatiles from Undamaged Eucalyptus Hosts Do Not Influence Psyllid Orientation

method: behavioural: single-insect Y-tube olfactometer, undamaged host-plant volatiles against clean air
conditions: Glass Y-tube olfactometer (8 cm test arms, 12 cm middle arm), a choice scored when a psyllid reached 4 cm into an arm within 30 min, undamaged host-foliage odour (Eucalyptus globulus juvenile and adult foliage, E. kitsoniana, E. camaldulensis across the four psyllid species) against an empty oven-bag clean-air arm; non-parametric binomial test against 50:50. Colonies of C. eucalypti, C. bipartita and A. bundoorensis were started from insects collected at La Trobe University (Bundoora) and Fish Creek, Victoria, and kept on potted hosts in a 24 C glasshouse; the fourth species, Glycaspis brimblecombei, was collected from field trees on test days. 'A minimum of 50 insects were tested in each experiment'; per-species n is shown only in Figure 2 (not read). Responsiveness 77 % (C. eucalypti), 74 % (C. bipartita), 70 % (A. bundoorensis), 69 % (G. brimblecombei). Null for undamaged host odour: the abstract says adult C. eucalypti were repelled by odours of damaged host leaves, and the next Results sentence says G. brimblecombei strongly avoided host odours (p < 0.001), so a null here is not a lack of olfactory ability; a pilot with damaged E. globulus juvenile leaves showed psyllids could respond to odours. A non-significant binomial test does not establish non-detection.
quote: Surprisingly, none of the four species were attracted to their host odors; C. eucalypti (p = 0.76), C. bipartita (p = 0.27), A. bundoorensis (p = 0.78).
